display.title: True to His Word
display.summary_short: A young couple gives away their wedding money to save a Jewish family, and the Baal Shem Tov's 'joking' wedding gifts come true. A lesson that a tzaddik's words about Moshiach will come true too.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins with the Rebbe's words, about thirty years ago, that the process of the Geulah has begun. Even if we do not yet see Moshiach, much has changed for the good, and when a tzaddik says something it comes true; our part is to add in mitzvos and learn about Moshiach. Then a Baal Shem Tov story: an innkeeper raises two orphaned young workers, Avraham and Sarah, arranges their marriage and gives them 600 gold coins to buy what they need. In the city they find a cruel poritz about to throw a Jewish family into a pit for unpaid rent, and they pay the whole debt. The innkeeper is proud and gives them the money again. At the wedding the Baal Shem Tov and his students arrive, and when the gifts are announced, they give a poritz's village, a lake, a flour mill and a forest. Everyone laughs. Later, running their own inn, the couple rescue a rich poritz's son on a stormy night. At the celebration, one poritz after another gives them exactly the gifts the Baal Shem Tov and his students announced.
display.lesson: When you do something for Hashem He repays much more, and a tzaddik's words always come true, including the Rebbe's promise that Moshiach is coming.

date.note: Says the Rebbe spoke about the Geulah 'about 30 years ago' and 'a little more than 30 years ago' (5751), so roughly 2021-2023.
